report:
Reviewed the complete transaction_isolation claim, seven ordinary implementation entries, the substantive domain-conflict test, and the explicit TODO test. The claim requires isolated speculative mutation, exclusive-leaf atomic commit, and rollback of equalities, bounds, universe refinements, wakes, tasks, and staged obligations on failure/cancellation. The source supports this transaction architecture; broad verification remains explicitly deferred as described below.

Implementation: unify.rs try_probe branches before invoking a fallible operation, rebuilds and collapses only after Ok, and discards on Err. try_unify_batch encloses every equality in the same child; try_set_bound includes universe checking and bound mutation in that transaction. try_unify_required similarly branches and discards, reading recovery metadata before rollback. Recursive unification, occurs checking, domain intersection, and make_accessible operate on the supplied child version. egraph.rs keeps parents, bounds, domains, universe ceilings, worklist, dependencies, revision, and wakes in per-version sparse state. Reads follow ancestry, not siblings; discard removes the version subtree and clears each removed state. collapse_into requires a direct, exclusive leaf, then merges the complete state and reowns child variables; only that path returns CommitEffects. version.rs prevents non-leaf mutation, allocates globally unique append-only identities, checks variable-owner ancestry, and tombstones removed nodes. Consequently discarded child variables do not become parent-visible.

boundary.rs validates malformed response metadata before branching, applies all response substitutions inside one child, and returns the copied certainty/output/modulo only after collapse. Any application error discards the child. No responses return empty effects. Placeholder registration records immutable identity metadata, while flexible universe lowering is version-local. prove.rs creates independent QueryProofState values for candidate tasks, branches candidate matching, extracts self-contained answers, then discards each candidate child. Candidate futures own their state, so dropping a canceled future also drops its private graph. Conjunction/existential inference uses child versions and discards on No; successful or uncertain common information is explicitly committed by their solver result protocol. runtime.rs ScopedTasks::cancel_all drops every future and resets the ready queue; Drop delegates to that cleanup. ProofFuture drop unsubscribes, and the whiteboard removes an abandoned producer and its queue entry when its last subscriber disappears. infer_ctx.rs publishes commit effects only after successful response application; failed application returns before wake publication. publish_obligation_batch consumes explicit staged data; the captured StagedObligationBatch helper owns only a vector, so a dropped unpublished batch has no publication effect. These essential lifecycle/publication files now have direct associations. Captured skeleton/bound helpers provide structural traversal and immutable bound descriptions without a separate mutation channel.

Tests: incompatible_transitive_domain_union_rolls_back first commits Any=Integer, then attempts the conflicting Float union. It asserts the exact Integer/Float DomainConflict, unchanged representatives on both classes, retained Integer domain, and unchanged parent revision. These visible assertions substantively verify preservation of an existing transitive class on failed speculation; a leaked union/domain/revision would fail. The cfg(test) evidence is an ordinary enabled unit test. I ran cargo test -p sage-ir incompatible_transitive_domain_union_rolls_back: one test passed. cargo fmt and cargo build also succeeded (existing warnings).

The second entry, sage_meta::todo::inference_transaction_isolation, is an empty, explicitly deferred verification matrix, not a passing behavioral test. It lists failed occurs/universe checks, multi-entry imports, candidate matching, cancellation/no-wake behavior, and concurrent sibling isolation. This remains an accepted test deferral: complete claim-wide automated verification requires focused fixtures that snapshot parent equality/bounds/universes and observe wake, task and staged-obligation publication across those failure/cancellation paths. In particular the substantive domain test does not assert task cancellation, staged obligation dropping, bound rollback, or every universe failure. Source inspection accounts for those mechanisms; no claim is made that the existing annotated test set executes the entire matrix. Existing unannotated unit checks were read as surrounding source, not counted as this anchor's associated test evidence. No implementation or test status was converted to hide a gap. No behavioral defect was reproduced during this review. Central delegated quality/sanity reviews for the association edits remain the coordinator's separate responsibility.
